AdmonitionNode.description:
A callout ("Note", "Warning"). ``kind`` is an open vocabulary; the
known values are ``KNOWN_ADMONITION_KINDS``.
AdmonitionNode.title: AdmonitionNode

BibEntry.description:
Bibliography pool entry — target of ``cites`` edges.

``formatted`` is the reference string as displayed in the built
document (the faithful capture). It is nullable because requiring it
presupposes a style engine ran, which a hand author or a markdown
producer has no reason to have. A curated typed subset of common
bibliographic fields is lifted alongside it; the full source entry
(e.g. Hayagriva) is carried losslessly as structured JSON in ``fields``.

An entry must carry ``formatted``, structured fields, or both — never an
empty, unconsumable entry. That floor is a validator rule, not a shape
the type system can express.
BibEntry.title: BibEntry

Cell.description: One cell of a ``table`` or a ``layout``; content is block nodes.
Cell.title: Cell

CiteRef.description: Forward citation edge; ``label`` resolves in the CND ``bibliography`` pool.
CiteRef.title: CiteRef

CodeNode.description:
Code block, verbatim. Inline code is a ``code`` mark. ``title`` is
the label an author gives a listing, typically a file name.
CodeNode.title: CodeNode

DocDate.description: Partial or full document date from cnd metadata.
DocDate.title: DocDate

DocMetadata.description:
Bibliographic metadata for the work the CND represents.

This identifies the *work* — title, authors, date. The input artifact it
was built from is ``Cnd.source``, deliberately separate: the same work
can be built from a Typst source and later re-imported from another
format (docs/proposals/0008).

``status`` and ``version`` are the values the author declares on the
document, unrelated to ``cnd_version`` and to any build history. ``extra``
holds any other title-page metadata; its keys never repeat a field name
(validation, docs/proposals/0013).
DocMetadata.title: DocMetadata

FigureNode.description:
Captioned/numbered wrapper; content keeps its own node type in
``children``. ``kind`` is the figure's category (open vocabulary),
useful above all for author-defined categories ``children`` cannot
reveal. ``description`` is the text equivalent of the visual. An
unconvertible body (a drawing) yields ``children=[]`` with ``raw``.
FigureNode.title: FigureNode

Footnote.description:
Footnote pool entry — target of ``footnotes`` edges. Its content is
block nodes: real nodes (global id/label uniqueness, location rule)
kept out of the body walk (docs/proposals/0013).
Footnote.title: Footnote

FootnoteRef.description: Forward footnote edge; ``label`` resolves in the CND ``footnotes`` pool.
FootnoteRef.title: FootnoteRef

HeadingNode.description: Section heading; the section's content is in ``children``.
HeadingNode.title: HeadingNode

LayoutNode.description: A grid used for arrangement only; position carries no relation.
LayoutNode.title: LayoutNode

LinkRef.description:
Forward hyperlink edge; ``href`` resolves nowhere in the CND.

The fourth forward family and the only one not keyed by label: a
hyperlink's target is outside the document by definition, so it admits
no resolution domain and has no dangling state — a URL is a URL. The
scheme is a consumer's business (``https:``, ``doi:``, an application
scheme); the format only carries the string.
LinkRef.title: LinkRef

ListItem.description:
One list entry. Its content is block nodes; a nested list is a
``list`` node with its own ``ordered``. ``checked`` is ``None`` for an
item that is not a task-list checkbox.
ListItem.title: ListItem

Mark.description:
A standoff span of inline formatting inside a ``RichText.value``.

``raw`` is the source of the covered text, used by ``math`` (the
readable linear form lives in ``value``, the formula here).
Mark.title: Mark

MathNode.description: Block equation. Inline math is a ``math`` mark.
MathNode.title: MathNode

NodeLocation.description:
Layout facts the SDK cannot derive from the tree: the page where the
node begins in the built document.

Nullable, because a page only exists for a paginated source. Pagination
is all-or-nothing across a CND — either every node carries a location or
none does — so ``location`` never encodes "unknown page" (docs/adr/0012,
docs/proposals/0008). Whether a CND is paginated is itself derived, not
serialized: see ``Cnd.paginated``.

Positions in reading order (document/sibling/page index and totals) are
NOT serialized — the node tree is normatively in reading order, so the
SDK derives them during traversal (see ``NodeTraverseContext``), the
same way reverse reference edges are derived (docs/adr/0008).
NodeLocation.title: NodeLocation

NodeRef.description:
Forward cross-reference edge to another node.

An edge is ``{label, text_span?}``: it names its target by label and
resolves through the CND's label index (docs/adr/0017, superseding the
``{id, label}`` form of docs/adr/0002). ``text_span`` marks where the
reference marker sits in the ``value`` of the ``RichText`` that holds
the edge, as a ``[start, end)`` pair of Unicode code-point offsets
(docs/adr/0013).
NodeRef.title: NodeRef

Numbering.description:
A resolved counter as displayed: ``value`` ("3", "2.1.1", "(1)")
and the counter word in the document's language (``name``, "Figure").

Replaces the flat ``number`` + ``counter_label`` pair, so a word
without a number can no longer be written (docs/proposals/0013).
Numbering.title: Numbering

ParagraphNode.description: A paragraph: the leaf that carries prose.
ParagraphNode.title: ParagraphNode

QuoteNode.description: Block quotation. An inline quotation stays text in its paragraph.
QuoteNode.title: QuoteNode

RawSource.description:
The producer's verbatim source for a node, with its language.

A bare string dropped the one thing a consumer needs to decide whether
to attempt a parse: which language the content is in. ``format`` is an
open string (``"typst"``, ``"latex"``, ``"mathml"``…), never a closed
enum — a new producer must not require a spec revision.
RawSource.title: RawSource

RichText.description:
Prose: a text, its language, its marks and its forward edges.

An edge belongs to the text in which its marker opens; its owning
node is the nearest node holding the text. Every list defaults to
empty and may be omitted, so ``{"value": "…"}`` is a complete text.
``lang`` null inherits from the enclosing text, then the node chain,
then ``doc.lang``.
RichText.title: RichText

SourceInfo.description:
The input artifact the CND was built from.

``hash`` is self-describing (``"sha256:…"``). Its comparability is
narrow and normative: two hashes are comparable only between CNDs from
the **same producer over the same source**, where equal means unchanged
and different means changed. Comparing across producers is meaningless.

``uri`` is an identifier in the producer's own space and is **never
promised resolvable** — a consumer must not dereference it.
SourceInfo.title: SourceInfo

TableNode.description:
A table whose rows and columns carry meaning. ``kind`` states what
it is: ``"data"`` (a dataset of records), ``"content"`` (cells to
read), ``None`` (unstated). Open vocabulary; never guessed by a
producer. A captioned table is wrapped in a ``FigureNode``.
TableNode.title: TableNode

TermItem.description: One term and its definition (block nodes in ``children``).
TermItem.title: TermItem

description: Top-level CND — a compiled document as a tree of typed nodes.
title: CND
